news.titleTr: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent relocated after alleged Iranian threats
news.summaryTr: Bessent is now one of several Trump administration officials to live on military bases due to safety concerns.
news.articleText: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent relocated after alleged Iranian threats - Published US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has been moved from his Washington DC home to a military base after Iran-linked threats to his life, according to US media reports. CBS, the BBC's US partner, said the relocation came after a photo of Bessent's home was published in the Wall Street Journal. Bessent has been at the forefront of efforts to isolate Iran economically through sanctions and a wider economic blockade. While the exact nature of the threats against Bessent remain unclear, US intelligence has warned that Iran has "substantially increased" efforts to target Americans, including US officials. "After the Wall Street Journal published an article featuring an online photo that allowed the location of the secretary's Georgetown home to be geo-located, security concerns began to increase," a source told CBS. Georgetown is an affluent part of Washington that is home to a number of government officials and prominent residents. Those security concerns, the source added, prompted authorities to move Bessent to a military base in the area. In a statement, a Treasury Department spokesperson said only that Bessent "will not be deterred" by threats and "remains committed" to the US effort to pressure Iran's economy. The BBC has contacted the White House for comment. In September, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned that Iran has "substantially increased" efforts to target Americans. The New York Times has reported that the Iranian effort includes the targeting of current and former US officials. One source told the newspaper this has "reached a more advanced stage". Other US officials reportedly on Iran's list of potential targets include former Secretary of State Mike Pompeo, former National Security Advisor John Bolton and Mark Milley, the former chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. Milley and Bolton's security teams were taken away by the Trump administration shortly after he returned to office last year. Bessent is one of a number of administration officials that live on military bases. The White House's new chief of staff, Stephen Miller, was moved to a base in late 2025 - before the conflict with Iran began. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio both live on military bases, as did former Attorney General Pam Bondi and former intelligence chief Tulsi Gabbard. The US and Israel launched an air campaign against Iran in February, killing its leader and prompting the regime in Tehran to retaliate with strikes on US allies across the region and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, through which around a fifth of the world's oil and gas usually travels. In June, the US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the strait, but it collapsed within weeks after Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated a blockade targeting Iranian ports. news.titleTr: Bitcoin hovers near $74K as stocks rise despite US bond yield rebound
news.summaryTr: Bitcoin traded in a narrow range as investors bought the dip in tech stocks and US bond yields climbed on high CPI inflation data.
news.articleText: Bitcoin hovers near $74K as stocks rise despite US bond yield rebound Bitcoin traded in a narrow range as investors bought the dip in tech stocks and US bond yields climbed on high CPI inflation data. Bitcoin (BTC) circled $74,000 at Wednesday’s Wall Street open as stock markets rallied and US bond yields surged. Key points: - Bitcoin failed to follow US stocks higher as CoreWeave gained up to 21% after beating Q3 revenue estimates. - The US 10-year bond yield hit a high of 5.02% on the back of higher-than-expected US CPI inflation. - BTC traded in a narrow range between its 21-week and 50-week trend lines at $73,078 and $75,492, respectively. Tech stocks rise while 10-year yield returns to 5% Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD diverging from US equities as investors resumed buying the dip in tech stocks. BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView The AI sector led the day’s early gains, with cloud-computing company CoreWeave jumping over 20% after reporting better-than-expected Q3 revenue and lifting its 2026 guidance. CoreWeave stock one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView Nvidia, which suffered on Monday and Tuesday amid ongoing controversy over CEO Jensen Huang, opened around 2.5% higher. Nvidia stock one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView Oil prices, meanwhile, gained on the day amid fading optimism over a diplomatic solution to the US-Iran war. As attacks on ships traversing the Strait of Hormuz continued, analysis pointed to several practical hurdles to restoring pre-conflict traffic levels, even if a deal is reached. “Even in the event a deal is struck, an increase in flows through the waterway would still depend on mine clearance, insurance costs and whether or not shipowners would even be willing to take the risk,” LSEG Oil Research wrote in a note on Tuesday, according to Reuters. US WTI crude oil was up 1.4% on the day at $87.70 per barrel after dropping to $84 on Tuesday, its lowest since late August. Brent crude gained 1.5% to $93.40. CFDs on WTI crude oil one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView Stocks rose even after Tuesday’s higher-than-expected Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation data pushed US bond yields sharply higher. The 10-year yield returned to 5% on Wednesday for the first time since Oct. 29, while the 30-year yield reached as high as 5.378%, a level last seen on Oct. 22. US 10-year bond yield one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView Peter Boockvar, chief investment officer at One Point BFG Wealth Partners, said that bonds were pricing in a more hawkish approach to interest rates by the US Federal Reserve. Markets have priced in a 0.25% rate hike in December, with the odds of a 0.5% move now increasing. “Inflation breakevens today are focused on the drop in oil prices while regular Treasuries today are reacting to a Fed that is definitely going to hike next month, as of now, with one another in January,” Boockvar told CNBC. Related: Here’s what happened in crypto today BTC price stays between two key trend lines Bitcoin continued to trade in a narrow range between its 21-week and 50-week simple moving average at $73,078 and $75,492, respectively. news.summaryTr: Clients can store and transfer Bitcoin, Ether and select stablecoins through the bank, which manages their wallets and private keys.
news.articleText: Deutsche Bank launches crypto custody for companies and institutions Clients can store and transfer Bitcoin, Ether and select stablecoins through the bank, which manages their wallets and private keys. Germany’s largest lender, Deutsche Bank, launched its crypto custody service for institutional and corporate clients on Wednesday, according to an announcement shared with Cointelegraph. The bank also signed a memorandum of understanding with Deutsche Asset Management, its majority-owned asset manager, to explore collaboration on tokenized money market funds, crypto asset exchange-traded commodities and stablecoins. Deutsche Bank announced plans to offer the service to institutional and corporate clients in Europe on Sept. 16, pending regulatory clearance. Deutsche Bank’s listing for crypto custody and transfer services in the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) register is dated Oct. 12 and names Germany’s BaFin as its regulator. The service initially supports Bitcoin (BTC), Ether (ETH) and select stablecoins, including Circle’s USDC (USDC) and EURC (EURC), as well as AllUnity EURAU. Gerald Podobnik, co-head of Deutsche Bank’s corporate bank, told Reuters in October that the bank planned to launch in Germany before expanding to Asian financial centers in 2027. Deutsche Bank partnered with crypto infrastructure provider Taurus in 2023 to develop custody services after applying for a digital asset custody license in Germany. Related: Deutsche Bank-backed AllUnity launches Swiss franc stablecoin CHFAU

news.summary: Ueno’s collapse exposed the fragility of digital banking in Paraguay, as customers scrambled for access to their money and stablecoins offered a lifeline.

news.titleTr: Paraguay bank collapse shows stablecoins can offer a lifeline... of sorts
news.summaryTr: Ueno’s collapse exposed the fragility of digital banking in Paraguay, as customers scrambled for access to their money and stablecoins offered a lifeline.
news.articleText: Paraguay bank collapse shows stablecoins can offer a lifeline... of sorts Ueno’s collapse exposed the fragility of digital banking in Paraguay, as customers scrambled for access to their money and stablecoins offered a lifeline. The collapse of Paraguay’s digital lender Ueno Bank last week left nearly three million customers — roughly 60% of Paraguay’s adults — unable to access their accounts. Paraguay’s Central Bank placed Ueno into resolution on Nov. 3 after its solvency ratio fell below half the legally required minimum. An investigation uncovered questionable lending practices and deficiencies in credit documentation and accounting. The collapse also triggered a political crisis, with thousands taking to the streets to protest and President Santiago Peña attempting to resign before being impeached and arrested on charges of breach of trust and using his office for personal gain. Paraguay’s peer-to-peer crypto market immediately reflected the turmoil, with some sellers asking for a USDt premium of up to 13%. “USDt is a lifeline for hundreds millions of people in the world,” Tether chief executive Paolo Ardoino said. For many, the incident sparked uncertainty over savings, wages and the money needed to cover everyday expenses. With the local guaraní (PYG) currency falling 12.3% in a week, some turned to stablecoins to maintain the value of their funds, or just to keep payments moving along. David Eisenmann, founder and chief executive of Paraguayan crypto exchange X4T, tells Magazine the timing made the liquidity need even more pronounced. “The intervention came in the first days of the month,” he says, “exactly when salaries, rent and supplier invoices are due,” adding that many business owners “couldn’t make payroll.” For some, USDt was “suddenly the most liquid money” they had: “This week they learned that having an account isn’t the same as having access to your money.” But beyond another TradFi masterclass in the virtues of self-custody, Ueno’s collapse highlights the growing role of dollar-pegged stablecoins providing an alternative source of liquidity when traditional banks fail. Crypto as a source of liquidity Eisenmann says X4T processed more than $10 million in local on-ramp volume over the 30 days to early November, but some of that activity predated Ueno’s collapse. “The dollar began recovering against the guaraní in October,” he says, “and the Ueno news sped up a move that was already underway.” Related: Stablecoins can drain from banks and nations at lightning speed He says the activity “runs in both directions,” with some customers selling crypto for guaraníes or dollars to cover payments they could no longer make through Ueno, while “demand for USDt and USDC as a dollar store of value has risen sharply.” Paraguay’s Central Bank placed Ueno into resolution on Nov. 3. Source: Central Bank of Paraguay As of Nov. 9 the Central Bank said 93.1% of customers with Ueno deposits had been repaid. Despite this confidence has been shaken and X4T continued to see higher online inquiries for dollar-denominated stablecoins. In fact, Eisenmann says the level “has not changed significantly” from the week of the collapse. Rhys Hicks, associate analyst at data and analytics company GlobalData, says the digital bank’s failure has shown “how much can go wrong when governance does not keep pace with growth.” That said, he’s not seeing evidence of a mass migration from Paraguayan banks into stablecoins, since other banks “picked up the slack,” and people “seem to have been angrier” with the government than with the banks. “Some consumers will look for different ways to keep their money safe, but I do not see an overwhelming shift to stablecoins yet,” he says. An old impulse, with new rails Seeking dollars when confidence in domestic banks falters is hardly new. In Argentina’s 2001 financial crisis, the government imposed the “corralito,” restricting cash withdrawals from bank accounts, following a run on deposits. Related: Peter Thiel backs crypto-friendly Silicon Valley Bank rival — Report Amid a deepening crisis over the country’s currency peg and sovereign debt, the government later converted dollar-denominated deposits into pesos, reducing people’s savings by about 30% overnight and further damaging confidence in the country’s fraying banking system. Tether CEO calls USDt a lifeline. Source: Paolo Ardoino But stablecoins aren’t decentralized and they are not insulated from the banking system either. During the March 2023 collapse of Silicon Valley Bank, stablecoin issuer Circle disclosed that $3.3 billion of USDC reserves, around 8% of the total, were held at the lender. USDC briefly depegged and fell to 86 cents on secondary markets after Circle said it could not withdraw the funds. A BIS paper on stablecoins and the international monetary system warns that widespread use of dollar-backed tokens could create challenges for monetary sovereignty in emerging markets. Hicks says stablecoins can provide an alternative during periods of political instability and “low trust in the local system” because they are pegged to a more stable currency, like the US dollar. But regulators need to address “transparency” and “consumer protection,” he says, because stablecoin holders don’t benefit from the same deposit guarantees as bank customers, and there is no central bank to step in and make them whole. Eisenmann says he expects the incident to spark more “diversification,” with people “spreading their money across banks, cash and digital assets” instead of relying on a single institution. “How quickly trust in the banks returns will depend on how quickly and transparently the authorities handle the resolution,” he says. news.summary: OP_CCV embeds contract state directly into Taproot output keys and enforces valid state transitions onchain. This makes it possible to achieve stateful contracts and compact fraud proofs.

news.titleTr: Bitcoin Covenants Part 5: MATT and OP_CHECKCONTRACTVERIFY — How Bitcoin could carry state across transactions
news.summaryTr: OP_CCV embeds contract state directly into Taproot output keys and enforces valid state transitions onchain. This makes it possible to achieve stateful contracts and compact fraud proofs.
news.articleText: Bitcoin Covenants Part 5: MATT and OP_CHECKCONTRACTVERIFY — How Bitcoin could carry state across transactions OP_CCV embeds contract state directly into Taproot output keys and enforces valid state transitions onchain. This makes it possible to achieve stateful contracts and compact fraud proofs. This is Part 5 in the technical article series about Bitcoin covenants by Cointelegraph Research. To read the previous article click here. MATT (Merkleize All The Things) is a smart contract framework for Bitcoin that enables stateful contracts and scalable fraud proofs. A stateful contract carries information forward across multiple transactions and can update this information as the contract evolves. Standard Bitcoin scripts do not provide this capability, because each transaction is evaluated independently with no memory of previous executions. Every covenant proposal allows state-carrying UTXOs to an extent, as illustrated by scripting languages such as Sapio, which builds on OP_CTV. This works by using addresses to represent a finite state automaton, where transactions function as the state transitions. However, there is no way to elegantly implement numerical logic in this paradigm, a gap filled by MATT, and in particular its proposed implementation through OP_CCV. Because MATT allows committed data to be computed at spend time and re-embedded into the next output, each spend can derive a new state dynamically, instead of choosing from a predetermined set of states. How OP_CCV commits state into a Taproot key To understand the MATT proposal, it is useful to first review how Taproot commits data through public keys. Every Taproot output contains a base public key, called the internal key, which can be cryptographically modified or “tweaked” to commit to extra information. Formally, the tweaked public key is Q = P + t·G, where P is the internal key, G is the generator of the secp256k1 elliptic curve, and t is a tagged hash of P and the committed data. In a regular Taproot output, this commitment typically encodes the Merkle root of a taptree, which contains hidden spending paths. MATT builds on this mechanism to also embed contract state into the key. Instead of embedding complex logic directly in Bitcoin’s scripting language, MATT encodes computation as a sequence of state commitments, and the chain verifies only that each state transition is valid. MATT can be realized through different opcode combinations. The most direct and well-specified implementation relies on OP_CHECKCONTRACTVERIFY (OP_CCV). OP_CCV provides the primitive that makes state-carrying UTXOs feasible within Taproot. OP_CCV allows a script to verify that a Taproot input or output key has been tweaked to commit to a specific piece of state data. The internal key is first tweaked with a hash of the contract’s current state, and then Taproot’s standard taptree tweak is applied on top. The resulting output key therefore commits to both the tapscript (the set of spending conditions) and the current state of the contract. OP_CCV can then enforce what state is carried forward into the next output. It allows the script to inspect the state data provided on the witness stack, perform computations on it, and require that the resulting updated state is correctly re-committed in a specified output. This is how state transitions are enforced on-chain. The stack format is: OP_CHECKCONTRACTVERIFY The opcode supports three modes for checking an output as well as a separate input mode. In default mode, the entire BTC value of the input UTXO is allocated to the specified output; in deduct mode, only a portion equal to the output’s amount is assigned, leaving the remainder available for further outputs; and in ignore mode, the script and data commitment are verified without constraining the amount. Because default and deduct modes are designed to preserve value across checked outputs, transaction fees must be paid through separate fee-paying inputs. A dedicated fee input and change output can be added to the transaction without conflicting with the covenant’s constraints. This prevents the accidental burning of funds that can occur in more primitive covenant implementations, such as OP_CTV or SIGHASH_ANYPREVOUT. It also addresses a major limitation of presigned-transaction-style covenants, which typically define amounts upfront and therefore cannot accommodate dynamic fee adjustments or partial unvaults. OP_CCV + OP_CAT: Merkle Proofs and Fraud Proofs When OP_CCV is combined with OP_CAT, the full MATT framework becomes even more expressive. OP_CAT enables byte concatenation in Script, which makes it possible to construct and verify Merkle proofs directly on-chain. Two distinct Merkle trees are associated with a Taproot output in such an arrangement. The first is the familiar Taproot script tree (the taptree), whose leaves are the contract’s spending scripts. The second is a separate state tree, whose leaves are the contract’s data, such as the intermediate steps of a computation. The OP_CCV + OP_CAT script can verify a Merkle proof against the current state tree root, compute the updated root after a transition, and use OP_CCV to force the next output to commit to it. This construction enables fraud-proof systems with a slashing condition in which a long computation is committed off-chain, and only the specific disputed step (with its path in the binary tree) needs to be revealed and verified on-chain. Similar systems exist as optimistic rollups on other blockchain systems: the full computation runs off-chain, and the on-chain contract only intervenes when someone raises a challenge. Fraud proofs require that the computation be compiled down to a binary circuit or equivalent step-by-step representation that can be committed to in a Merkle tree. OP_CCV + OP_CAT would avoid the need for the Lamport one-time signatures and pre-signed transaction graphs that BitVM relies on to enforce state consistency. Beyond fraud proofs, the OP_CCV and OP_CAT combination also has implications for vaults. OP_CCV alone can implement vaults, but when combined with OP_CAT, it allows fully featured vaults that are essentially equivalent to the functionality proposed by OP_VAULT. As James O’Beirne, the author of OP_VAULT, has noted, OP_CCV represents a more general and robust design that effectively supersedes his earlier proposal. In the next article in this series, we will move on from general covenant proposals to review application-specific opcodes such as OP_VAULT, OP_UNVAULT, and OP_EVICT. Each of the opcodes are designed to solve a specific problem rather than provide broad programmability. Magazine: Bitcoin holders have received eCash — What can you do with it?

Its revenue backlog reached $132.5 billion. CoreWeave shares jumped 15.27% in premarket trading Wednesday after the AI cloud provider reported third-quarter revenue that beat analyst estimates. The shares traded at $56.12 as of 12:50 pm UTC, trimming the stock’s year-to-date decline to 32%, according to Yahoo Finance. CoreWeave reported $3.66 billion in third-quarter revenue after the market closed on Tuesday, up 168% from $1.36 billion a year earlier. Revenue came in about 3.4% above the $3.54 billion consensus estimate compiled by Google Finance. The company also reported a revenue backlog of about $132.5 billion as of Sept. 30. The figure includes revenue CoreWeave expects to recognize under existing customer contracts, subject to delivery and service availability. In April, CoreWeave announced a multiyear agreement with AI developer Anthropic to provide computing capacity for its Claude models. Days later, CoreWeave signed a $6 billion deal with quantitative trading company Jane Street to supply cloud infrastructure for trading and research. CoreWeave started as a crypto miner and began shifting to AI infrastructure in 2019. Related: CoreWeave shows how crypto-era infrastructure quietly became AI’s backbone

news.title: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
news.articleText: Release Number 9324-26 CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers November 09, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced eight orders filing and settling charges against Michael Talento, Anthony Tyler Williams, Quillan Roberto Black, Christopher Williams, Michael Levi Peters, Jordan Taylor Morgan, Lewis Matthew Neal, and Tyler Evan MacKechnie for acting as unregistered associated persons of unregistered foreign introducing brokers. According to the orders, the introducing brokers engaged in the solicitation of orders for off-exchange leveraged or margined retail foreign currency and retail commodities transactions with U.S. customers who were not eligible contract participants. The respondents solicited those customers without registering as associated persons of the introducing brokers, as required. Under the orders, the respondents must cease and desist from engaging in their illegal conduct. They also are barred for two years from registering with the Commission in any capacity or acting as a principal, agent, or employee of any CFTC registrant. Each order also recognizes the penalty the respondent owes in a related Securities and Exchange Commission proceeding. These orders relate to a prior Commission order sanctioning Netrios LP Ltd. and Red Acre Ltd. for facilitating illegal off-exchange commodity transactions with U.S. customers. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9263-26] The SEC has filed and settled charges against the respondents based on the same underlying conduct. The CFTC thanks the SEC for its assistance. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
news.articleText: Release Number 9323-26 CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an interpretation (“Interpretation”) of the requirement that designated contract markets (“DCMs”) provide competitive, open, fair, and impartial access to their members and persons with trading privileges under Commission Regulation 38.151(b) (“Impartial Access Requirements”). “Derivatives markets must operate on a uniform basis at a national scale in order to achieve the purposes set out in the Commodity Exchange Act,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with those purposes and the Act’s impartial access requirements.” DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions that violate the Impartial Access Requirements within 30 days, or else submit to the Division of Market Oversight (“Division”) an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. Further, within 30 days, DCMs should ensure that intermediaries accessing their markets are not impeding and are complying with the DCM’s Impartial Access Requirements, or else submit to the Division an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. The Commission will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case in connection with potential Commission action. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
news.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
news.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
news.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-

news.title: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
news.articleText: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig addressed conference attendees, “I have spent a lot of time this year traveling around the country and talking to farmers and ranchers working hard each day to provide the food, feed, and fiber we depend on throughout our country and the world. I’ve met with farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and energy producers in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and Florida, and now, I’m with all of you here in Kansas.” [Watch Chairman Selig’s full remarks here.] Following Chairman Selig’s remarks, panelists examined the relationship between cash and derivatives markets, evolving commodity contracts, and the importance of effective hedging tools for agricultural producers. There were also panels where industry representatives addressed access to agricultural credit and the financial challenges facing producers and merchants. Additional afternoon discussions focused on rising production costs, fluctuating commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, and broader pressures on the farm economy. In addition, conference participants engaged in discussions about emerging market developments, including perpetual futures, 24/7 trading, and tokenized collateral, and their implications for agricultural risk management. CFTC Chief Advisor Alex Titus and White House Council of Economic Advisers Member Aaron Hedlund also examined the U.S. economic outlook, agricultural trade, and policies shaping American agriculture. The first day concluded with a keynote address from U.S. Department of Agriculture Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. U.S. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas opened the second day with a morning keynote address on agricultural policy and legislative priorities facing American producers. The morning continued with discussions on agricultural prediction markets, the use of data in modern commodity markets, and developments in event contracts. In addition, panelists examined superintelligence, information advantages, and market integrity, including the implications of emerging technologies for market participants and regulators. Chairman Selig joined Futures Industry Association President and CEO Walt Lukken for a fireside chat examining the Commission’s priorities, the evolving regulatory landscape, and developments shaping derivatives markets. The conference concluded with discussions on enhancing public understanding of markets through data and customer education, followed by a panel examining clearing, market access, and the role of intermediaries in derivatives markets. Chairman Selig delivered closing remarks, concluding AgCon2026. -CFTC-
news.articleTextTr: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig addressed conference attendees, “I have spent a lot of time this year traveling around the country and talking to farmers and ranchers working hard each day to provide the food, feed, and fiber we depend on throughout our country and the world. I’ve met with farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and energy producers in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and Florida, and now, I’m with all of you here in Kansas.” [Watch Chairman Selig’s full remarks here.] Following Chairman Selig’s remarks, panelists examined the relationship between cash and derivatives markets, evolving commodity contracts, and the importance of effective hedging tools for agricultural producers. There were also panels where industry representatives addressed access to agricultural credit and the financial challenges facing producers and merchants. Additional afternoon discussions focused on rising production costs, fluctuating commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, and broader pressures on the farm economy. In addition, conference participants engaged in discussions about emerging market developments, including perpetual futures, 24/7 trading, and tokenized collateral, and their implications for agricultural risk management. CFTC Chief Advisor Alex Titus and White House Council of Economic Advisers Member Aaron Hedlund also examined the U.S. economic outlook, agricultural trade, and policies shaping American agriculture. The first day concluded with a keynote address from U.S. Department of Agriculture Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. U.S. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas opened the second day with a morning keynote address on agricultural policy and legislative priorities facing American producers. The morning continued with discussions on agricultural prediction markets, the use of data in modern commodity markets, and developments in event contracts. In addition, panelists examined superintelligence, information advantages, and market integrity, including the implications of emerging technologies for market participants and regulators. Chairman Selig joined Futures Industry Association President and CEO Walt Lukken for a fireside chat examining the Commission’s priorities, the evolving regulatory landscape, and developments shaping derivatives markets. The conference concluded with discussions on enhancing public understanding of markets through data and customer education, followed by a panel examining clearing, market access, and the role of intermediaries in derivatives markets. Chairman Selig delivered closing remarks, concluding AgCon2026. -CFTC-

items.articleText: İki üniversiteden 40 akademik personel alımı! Başvurular başladı - Acıbadem Üniversitesi 25, Doğuş Üniversitesi 15 olmak üzere iki üniversite toplam 40 akademik personel alacak. Profesör, doçent, doktor öğretim üyesi ve araştırma görevlisi kadroları için başvuru ve sınav takvimi açıklandı. İstanbul'daki Acıbadem Mehmet Ali Aydınlar Üniversitesi ve Doğuş Üniversitesi, toplam 40 akademik personel istihdam etmek üzere ilana çıktı. Profesör, doçent, doktor öğretim üyesi, öğretim görevlisi ve araştırma görevlisi kadrolarını kapsayan alımlarda son başvuru tarihleri ve aranan şartlar açıklandı. Acıbadem Üniversitesi 25 akademisyen alacak CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Acıbadem Mehmet Ali Aydınlar Üniversitesi, 18 öğretim üyesi ile 7 öğretim görevlisi ve araştırma görevlisi olmak üzere toplam 25 kişilik kadro açtı. Üniversitenin öğretim üyesi alımları kapsamında 7 profesör, 3 doçent ve 8 doktor öğretim üyesi istihdam edilecek. Kadroların bulunduğu alanlar arasında şunlar yer alıyor: - Genel cerrahi - Ortopedi ve travmatoloji - Kulak burun boğaz - Kardiyoloji - Moleküler biyoloji ve genetik - Bilgisayar mühendisliği - Beslenme ve diyetetik - Gastronomi Üniversite ayrıca radyasyon onkolojisi ve patoloji laboratuvar teknikleri alanlarında öğretim görevlisi; eczacılık, hemşirelik, beslenme ve diyetetik ile medikal biyoteknoloji alanlarında araştırma görevlisi alacak. Öğretim üyeliği kadrolarına başvuruların ilan tarihinden itibaren 15 gün içinde şahsen yapılması gerekiyor. Öğretim görevlisi ve araştırma görevlisi kadroları için son başvuru tarihi 26 Kasım 2026 olarak açıklandı. Bu kadrolara başvuracak adayların ALES'ten en az 70 puan alması gerekiyor. Yabancı dille eğitim veren bölümlerde ise yabancı dil puanına ilişkin ek koşullar aranacak. Doğuş Üniversitesi 15 kişilik kadro açtı Doğuş Üniversitesi, 9 öğretim üyesi ve 6 öğretim görevlisi olmak üzere toplam 15 akademik personel istihdam edecek. Öğretim üyesi alımları şu alanlarda gerçekleştirilecek: - Hukuk - Psikoloji - Uluslararası ticaret ve işletmecilik - Siyaset bilimi ve kamu yönetimi - Görsel iletişim tasarımı - Hemşirelik - Yazılım geliştirme - Endüstri mühendisliği Üniversitenin meslek yüksekokulunda ise mekatronik, dijital dönüşüm elektroniği, robotik ve yapay zekâ, imalat yürütme sistemleri operatörlüğü ile internet ve ağ teknolojileri programlarına öğretim görevlisi alınacak. Öğretim görevlisi kadrolarına başvuracak adayların ALES'ten en az 70 puan almış ve ilgili alanlarda en az tezli yüksek lisans derecesine sahip olması gerekiyor. Başvuru tarihleri ve sınav takvimi açıklandı Doğuş Üniversitesi'nin akademik personel alımı için başvurular 12 Kasım'da başladı. Son başvuru tarihi 26 Kasım 2026 saat 17.00 olarak belirlendi. Doğuş Üniversitesi'nin sınav takvimi şöyle: - 30 Kasım: Ön değerlendirme sonuçları - 1 Aralık: Giriş sınavı - 3 Aralık: Nihai sonuçların açıklanması Acıbadem Üniversitesi'nin öğretim görevlisi ve araştırma görevlisi kadroları için takvim ise şöyle: - 30 Kasım: Ön değerlendirme sonuçları - 2 Aralık: Giriş sınavı - 4 Aralık: Nihai sonuçların açıklanması Başvurular, üniversitelerin ilanlarında belirtilen ilgili birimlere şahsen veya izin verilen kadrolarda posta yoluyla yapılabilecek. İnternet üzerinden başvuru kabul edilmeyecek. İzmir Kâtip Çelebi Üniversitesi'nin ilanında değişiklik Öte yandan İzmir Kâtip Çelebi Üniversitesi de 2 Kasım 2026 tarihli öğretim üyesi alım ilanında değişikliğe gitti. Üniversite, İktisadi ve İdari Bilimler Fakültesi Sağlık Yönetimi Bölümü Hastane İşletmeciliği Ana Bilim Dalı için açılan 7 numaralı profesör kadrosunun şartlarını güncelledi. Aynı ilanda bulunan 18 numaralı öğretim üyesi kadrosu ise iptal edildi.

items.title: Zelenskiy'den üçlü zirve mesajı: Putin, Trump ve Kiev aynı masaya gelebilir
items.summary: Zelenskiy, Rusya-Ukrayna Savaşı'nı sona erdirmek için Trump, Putin ve kendisinin katılacağı üçlü zirveye yönelik görüşmelerin sürdüğünü açıkladı. Abu Dabi'deki müzakerelerde 1.200 esire kadar takas ve güvenlik garantileri de gündeme geldi.

items.titleTr: Zelenskiy'den üçlü zirve mesajı: Putin, Trump ve Kiev aynı masaya gelebilir
items.summaryTr: Zelenskiy, Rusya-Ukrayna Savaşı'nı sona erdirmek için Trump, Putin ve kendisinin katılacağı üçlü zirveye yönelik görüşmelerin sürdüğünü açıkladı. Abu Dabi'deki müzakerelerde 1.200 esire kadar takas ve güvenlik garantileri de gündeme geldi.
items.articleText: Zelenskiy'den üçlü zirve mesajı: Putin, Trump ve Kiev aynı masaya gelebilir - Zelenskiy, Rusya-Ukrayna Savaşı'nı sona erdirmek için Trump, Putin ve kendisinin katılacağı üçlü zirveye yönelik görüşmelerin sürdüğünü açıkladı. Abu Dabi'deki müzakerelerde 1.200 esire kadar takas ve güvenlik garantileri de gündeme geldi. Ukrayna Devlet Başkanı Volodimir Zelenskiy, Rusya ile savaşı sona erdirmek amacıyla ABD, Rusya ve Ukrayna liderlerini bir araya getirecek üçlü zirve için görüşmelerin sürdüğünü açıkladı. Abu Dabi'deki müzakerelerde esir takası, güvenlik garantileri ve enerji altyapılarına yönelik saldırıların durdurulması da gündeme geldi. Abu Dabi'de 1.200 esirin takası gündemde CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle İrlanda'nın başkenti Dublin'de Başbakan Micheal Martin ile bir araya gelen Zelenskiy, ortak basın toplantısında Rusya-Ukrayna Savaşı'na ilişkin diplomatik temasları değerlendirdi. Zelenskiy, 10-11 Kasım'da Birleşik Arap Emirlikleri'nin başkenti Abu Dabi'de ABD, Rusya ve Ukrayna heyetlerinin katılımıyla üçlü müzakereler gerçekleştirildiğini hatırlattı. Görüşmelerde tarafların biner esiri takas etmesi seçeneğinin ele alındığını belirten Zelenskiy, takasın 1.200 esire çıkarılmasının da mümkün olabileceğini söyledi. Ukrayna lideri, müzakerelerde ülkesine yönelik farklı güvenlik garantisi modellerinin de değerlendirildiğini ifade etti. Kiev'den enerji saldırıları ve denizde ateşkes önerisi Zelenskiy, Ukrayna'nın müzakerelerde Rusya'ya enerji altyapılarına yönelik saldırıların durdurulmasını ve denizde ateşkes sağlanmasını önerdiğini açıkladı. Ancak Rus heyetinin bu konularda karar verme yetkisi bulunmadığını savunan Zelenskiy, görüşmelerde henüz somut bir sonuca ulaşılamadığını belirtti. Putin ile görüşmede üçlü zirve gündeme gelecek Abu Dabi'deki görüşmelere katılan ABD'li yetkililerin 12 Kasım'da Rusya Devlet Başkanı Vladimir Putin ile bir araya gelmesi bekleniyor. Zelenskiy, ABD Başkanı Donald Trump'ın damadı ve Özel Temsilcisi Jared Kushner ile Trump'ın Özel Temsilcisi Steve Witkoff'un Putin'le yapacağı görüşmede üçlü zirve konusunu gündeme getirmesini beklediklerini söyledi. Ukrayna lideri, ABD, Rusya ve Ukrayna liderlerinin bir araya gelmesinin savaşın sona erdirilmesine ilişkin kritik başlıkların ele alınması açısından önemli olduğunu vurguladı. Üçlü zirvenin gerçekleştirilmesi ihtimalinin ve liderler düzeyinde görüşme için tarafların atması gereken adımların müzakere edildiğini belirten Zelenskiy, sürecin büyük ölçüde ABD ile Rusya arasındaki temaslara bağlı olduğunu ifade etti. Zelenskiy: Avrupa da müzakere masasında olmalı Ukrayna Devlet Başkanı, Avrupa ülkelerinin de barış görüşmelerinde yer alması gerektiğini söyledi. Zelenskiy, ABD tarafının Avrupa'nın sürece katılımına daha olumlu yaklaştığını belirtti. Zelenskiy ayrıca Dublin'deki temasları kapsamında Kushner ve Witkoff ile de görüşebileceğini açıkladı.

items.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, OKX and Intercontinental Exchange are preparing to launch tokenized stock trading on Nov. 23 despite objections from major companies, Barclays increased its holdings in BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF by 48% in the third quarter, and pro-crypto lawmaker Tom Emmer was elected House Republican minority whip as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress. OKXICE moves ahead with tokenized stocks as blue chips push back Crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) are set to launch tokenized stock trading on Nov. 23, despite objections from 67 companies to having their shares listed and warnings from Nasdaq that trading across disconnected platforms could fragment liquidity. The venture, known as OKXICE, will operate under the US Securities and Exchange Commission’s temporary Innovation Exemption and offer eligible US customers round-the-clock trading. Under the exemption, venues must give companies a chance to object before listing shares tokenized by an unaffiliated third party. JPMorgan Chase, McDonald’s, SpaceX and Coca-Cola were among the companies that objected. Tokenized stocks are blockchain-based tokens that represent company shares or track their price. The rights they carry depend on how they are structured. The distributed value of tokenized stocks and ETFs reached $3.88 billion on Nov. 11, up 13.4% over 30 days. In comments to Cointelegraph, former New York governor and OKXICE co-chair Andrew Cuomo said investors would have “the same rights, protections and ownership that come with the underlying shares.” Barclays boosts BlackRock Bitcoin ETF stake 48% as banks expand holdings Barclays reported holding 3.94 million shares in BlackRock’s spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) at the end of the third quarter, up 48% from the previous quarter. The position in the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) was worth about $187 million on Sept. 30, up from $88.5 million for 2.66 million shares on June 30, according to Barclays’ Friday Form 13F filing. “Early readings suggest longer-term holders make up a growing share of the spot bitcoin ETF investor base,” Bitwise analyst Camran Khosravi told Cointelegraph, pointing to increased bank exposure, including at Citigroup. Citigroup reported a new position worth about $119 million in the Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC). items.titleTr: Poundland set for more time to secure a rescue deal as emergency talks continue
items.summaryTr: The BBC understands the discount chain, which has been edging towards administration, will be given more time to find a buyer.
items.articleText: Poundland set for more time to secure a rescue deal as emergency talks continue - Published Poundland looks set to avoid immediate collapse after its US owners told MPs on Wednesday they were in favour of extending a deadline to find a rescue deal. The discount chain, which has 11,000 employees, has been edging towards administration after being blocked by Gordon Borthers from accessing cash in its bank accounts. A deadline to secure a buyer for the business is set to expire at midnight, but sources close to the situation told the BBC they expect more time will be given, thanks to the release of £10m in funding. A committee of MPs questioned Gordon Brothers following accusations that the investment firm hopes to profit from selling off Poundland's 600 stores and stock piecemeal. Gordon Brothers - which bought the chain for just £1 last year - is accused of forcing that outcome by restricting Poundland's access to available cash needed to restock stores and pay wages and rent, ahead of the crucial Christmas trading period. The investment firm, which specialises in buying and restructuring distressed companies, has denied the claims. But pressure remains on Poundland's owners after a takeover bid was rejected. The decision prompted calls for answers from politicians, including Prime Minister Andy Burnham. About £50m had been frozen by Gordon Brothers, the BBC understands, meaning Poundland bosses were unable to restock shelves across its 600 shops. However, sources close to the matter told the BBC on Tuesday that a release of £10m by its owners, while "small in the scale of things" could help at least postpone the chain's collapse while a longer term solution was explored. 'Do the right thing' Following the meeting between MPs on the business and trade committee and representatives of Gordon Brothers, chairman Liam Byrne told the BBC he was "deeply concerned" and described the firm's behaviour as "much like a wolf on Wall Street, on the British High Street". "They refused to prioritise, protecting jobs and stores over and above their own financial returns," he added. "It's clear that they've taken millions out of Poundland at a time when they themselves said the business was on a knife edge." Byrne said the committee's message to Gordon Brothers was to ensure Poundland had "access to the funds that it needs to trade at what should be one of the busiest periods in the year". He urged Gordon Brothers to "do what is right to save jobs and stores and do that now". "It's a good business, it's a much-loved business, and particularly in the middle of the cost of living crisis, communities up and down the country rely on access to the kind of stores that it operates," Byrne added. Following the private meeting with MPs, Poundland's chief executive Barry Williams told the BBC the chain's board would hold an urgent meeting on Wednesday night. Views on Poundland performance differ The 10-day moratorium to protect Poundland from its creditors expires on Thursday, but if there is a prospect of a solvent deal, the deadline could be extended. Views on the chain's performance differ between those running operations and the owners. Poundland boss Williams told staff last week that like-for-like sales, which exclude new store openings, were up 11.4%. The sales period included Halloween, but Williams said this was £1.5m ahead of budget. He added the business made a profit of £18.1m in the year to September, which was a "strong recovery" from the previous year where there were losses of £68m. However, Gordon Brothers has painted a different picture, saying the chain remains "challenged and vulnerable to any potential downturn in future trading". It has argued the best way of securing jobs may be to split up the business and sell chunks of its 600 sites to other retailers. There has been interest from the likes of Poundstretcher, Tesco and B&M in picking up Poundland stores which could mean continuing employment for workers in the event the chain is broken up. The main issue is whether a piecemeal sale would protect more jobs than a buyer willing to keep Poundland as a national chain. Get in touch Are you affected by issues discussed in this story? items.titleTr: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike
items.summaryTr: Tens of thousands of people have been taking part in the strike, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living.
items.articleText: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike - Published Clashes have broken out between groups of masked men and police in Barcelona after tens of thousands of people took part in Spain's first general strike for 14 years, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living. Some 120,000 people joined a demonstration in the capital Madrid and more than 50,000 turned out in Barcelona, where footage showed masked men setting fire to rubbish bins and smashing shop windows as police fired tear gas. Transport and other public services across Spain faced serious disruption. Spaniards are due to vote in parliamentary elections on 29 November. The head of the big UGT labour union, Pepe Álvarez, said the strike was a success with "massive" participation, while Unai Sordo of the CC OO union said turnout was "very significant." There was a heavy police presence in the centre of Barcelona on Wednesday evening, with officers wearing helmets and riot shields. Some of the disturbances took place in the Passeig de Gràcia, close to the iconic Plaça de Catalunya in the centre of the city. Small fires burned in the middle of the streets as bins were set alight. Local media reported that a group of people fired fireworks towards police and looted shops including the Lego store. Protesters were also seen trying to enter the Apple Store. The BBC spoke to a woman who attended the protests in Barcelona who said it was mostly very peaceful and "joyful". She said she was there to protest about the housing costs and that "there were a lot of children and old people there." She was in the area of Las Ramblas in the evening and saw fires in the streets. "The fires were everywhere, it was very intense," she said. Earlier in the day there was major disruption around Madrid and Barcelona, with traffic halted on several main roads. The interior ministry said dozens of people were arrested for a variety of incidents and Spanish reports said estate agencies had seen attacks on their offices. "We've completely brought the city to a standstill," a protester in Madrid told Reuters news agency, adding there was widespread support for the general strike. "Everyone's out there, despite the rainy weather; everyone's out on the streets." Another protester, 37-year-old teacher Olga Domingo, said she was protesting because "the housing situation is outrageous. The current cost of living compared to wages is completely unsustainable". The strike was triggered by widespread protests over affordable housing and rising living costs, after the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal from a flat in Madrid where she had lived for seven decades. She died in hospital weeks later. Rental prices in the capital have risen in recent years. The monthly cost of a 50 sq m apartment in Madrid was an average of €1,170 ($1,300; £1,000) in October, according to property portal Idealista, while Spain's average gross monthly salary is about €2,460. That amounts to nearly half the average gross salary, well above the 30% level of affordability often recommended by housing experts and public institutions. Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called snap elections last month after parliament failed to approve his plan for housing reform. Not since 2012, under the conservative government of Mariano Rajoy, has Spain held general strikes. And while previous strikes have been problematic for the government in power, this one is different. Sánchez and his ministers have even encouraged workers to down tools and demand affordable housing. "Your eight-hour day. Your pension. Your public healthcare… These were collective conquests," he wrote on social media, praising those who took part in previous strikes. The conservative People's Party (PP), by contrast, has accused the government of attempting to weaponise the strike for electoral gain. PP leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo called the general strike "nonsense", calling the unions "mafia" and "trash". Feijoo's party is leading in the polls and party spokesman Miguel Tellado accused the government of exploiting the strike to warn voters against allowing a right-wing government to be formed, which looks the most likely outcome of the 29 November election. Sánchez told Spanish TV this week: "What is nonsense is to question the rights of workers to strike." Among those taking part in the general strike was Gonzalo Álvarez, 27, who was visiting different picket lines in central Madrid. Although he works in sales, he has been volunteering for a housing union that tries to protect tenants and makes them aware of their rights. The eviction of Maricarmen Abascal at the end of September "was the little fire" that sparked this protest, he told the BBC. Álvarez knew the 87-year-old, who had faced a tripling of her rent under new landlords, and says he was deeply upset by her treatment. He rents a small, one-bedroom flat with his girlfriend, a dental hygienist, in the city's southern Arganzuela disrict. The couple pay €1,000 between them, which means each spends about half of their salary on housing, even before other bills. "It's absolutely crazy… with the food, with the electricity, with the water, with gas." He sees no way of getting on the property ladder: "You have to collect an insane amount of money to be able to buy a house. So with these salaries, it's impossible." With current rent and purchase prices, he believes buying somewhere is "completely impossible". However, the vice-president of the CEOE, Spanish biggest business association, Miguel Garrido, criticised the strike, complaining that businesses had little to do with the price of housing. "This is not a strike for labour-related reasons, but rather for political ones, and it is closely linked to the early calling of elections," he said. Demonstrations were planned for some of Spain's biggest cities later in the day and the scale of support will be widely viewed as an indicator of public discontent ahead of the election. Another reliable indicator of support for strikes is the level of demand for electricity with Spain's industrial sector. Power usage in Spain fell by 7.5% during the early hours of Wednesday, according to data from operator Red Eléctrica. During the last general strike 14 years ago, equivalent consumption was down by more than 15%. Additional reporting by Gabriela Pomeroy Related topics Read more - Published23 September - Published5 October

items.title: Uncalled US House races could send more crypto allies to Congress
items.summary: The remaining races feature pro-crypto candidates and others without a stated position, giving advocacy groups what they see as “an opportunity” for outreach.

items.titleTr: Uncalled US House races could send more crypto allies to Congress
items.summaryTr: The remaining races feature pro-crypto candidates and others without a stated position, giving advocacy groups what they see as “an opportunity” for outreach.
items.articleText: Uncalled US House races could send more crypto allies to Congress The remaining races feature pro-crypto candidates and others without a stated position, giving advocacy groups what they see as “an opportunity” for outreach. Just over a week after a “blue wave” handed Democrats control of the US House and Senate, 14 races have yet to be called. The results so far have added crypto supporters in both chambers and the remaining races could bring more into Congress. Three candidates in the uncalled races received backing from crypto political action committees (PACs). According to Stand With Crypto, every candidate in those races is either strongly pro-crypto or has no stated position. As crypto advocacy groups look ahead to 2028, they’re turning their attention to candidates who have yet to take a public stance on crypto. House races still to be called Crypto PACs backed three candidates in US House races that remain undecided. Two incumbents lead in Alaska and North Carolina, while a Louisiana state senator faces a December runoff. Rep. Nick Begich leads in Alaska’s US House race. Defend American Jobs, Fairshake’s Republican-facing affiliate, backed him with $508,142 in the August primary. The same PAC put $150,600 behind Rep. David Rouzer, who leads in North Carolina’s 7th District. Louisiana state Sen. Blake Miguez will face Democrat Chauna Banks in a Dec. 12 runoff for the state’s 6th District. The Fellowship PAC backed Miguez with $250,000. The Associated Press called the race in South Carolina’s 2nd District for incumbent Rep. Joe Wilson on the morning of Nov. 11. Stand With Crypto rates Wilson as “strongly supportive of crypto.” His win brought the group’s House tally to 246 crypto supporters and 107 opponents, while the Senate stood at 50 supporters and 33 opponents. In the remaining races, Stand With Crypto lists each candidate as either strongly supportive of crypto or having no stated position. “The new members that have no stance present an opportunity,” Blockchain Association Chief Policy Officer Lindsay Fraser told Cointelegraph. Educating the incoming congress Nearly one in four members of the incoming Congress will be new, Fraser said, and many have given little thought to blockchain technology. “To us, that represents a blank slate in terms of education,” she said. Blockchain Association is planning a January fly-in to reach newly elected lawmakers. “Leaving the 120th Congress with more members in that A and B category would be a huge success,” she said, referring to Stand With Crypto’s ratings. The group gives an A to candidates who strongly support crypto and a B to those who are somewhat supportive. Fraser said age plays a bigger role than party affiliation in how lawmakers vote on crypto. She said members under 55 are much more likely to support the industry and that the incoming class skews younger. Fraser said she wants the industry to enter the 2028 election “with two candidates who […] are thoughtful in regards to the industry,” so the sector can avoid “living and dying by the outcome of that election.” Magazine: Wall Street killed Bitcoin’s wild rallies: 10x’s Markus Thielen

items.articleText: Katar'dan Hürmüz uyarısı: Krizin küresel ekonomiye faturası ağırlaşıyor - Katar, Hürmüz Boğazı'ndaki krizin enerji, taşımacılık ve gıda fiyatları üzerinden küresel kalkınmayı tehdit ettiğini açıkladı. Doha, 2025'te BM ile 21 milyon dolarlık iki anlaşma imzalarken 2027'de yeni bir kalkınma toplantısına ev sahipliği yapacak. Katar, Hürmüz Boğazı'ndaki aksaklıkların enerji, deniz taşımacılığı ve gıda güvenliği üzerinden küresel ekonomiye etkilerinin giderek ağırlaştığı uyarısında bulundu. Katar Uluslararası İşbirliğinden Sorumlu Devlet Bakanı Meryem bint Ali el-Misned, krizin özellikle gelişmekte olan ülkelerin kalkınma kazanımlarını tehdit ettiğini söyledi. Hürmüz'deki kriz enerji ve gıda fiyatlarına yansıyor CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Misned, Paris Barış Forumu kapsamında Doha Forumu işbirliğiyle düzenlenen “Hürmüz Boğazı'nın Kapatılmasının Etkileri: Çatışmanın Küresel Kalkınmaya Gizli Maliyeti” başlıklı oturumda konuştu. Boğazdaki aksaklıkların yalnızca enerji piyasalarıyla sınırlı kalmadığını belirten Misned, etkilerin yakıt ve deniz taşımacılığından gübre ve gıda fiyatlarına, oradan da hane halklarının bütçelerine kadar yayıldığını ifade etti. Bölgesel krizlerin küresel sonuçlar doğurduğuna dikkat çeken Misned, uluslararası işbirliğinin güçlendirilmesi gerektiğini vurguladı. Diplomasi, egemenliğe ve uluslararası hukuka saygı ile seyrüsefer özgürlüğünün bölgesel istikrar ve küresel refah açısından temel unsurlar olduğunu söyledi. IMF'nin büyüme ve enflasyon tahminlerine dikkat çekti Misned, Uluslararası Para Fonu'nun (IMF) tahminlerini de gündeme getirdi. Buna göre gelişmekte olan ve yükselen ekonomilerde büyümenin geçen yılki yüzde 4,5 seviyesinden bu yıl yüzde 3,7'ye gerilemesi, küresel enflasyonun ise yüzde 4,7'ye yükselmesi bekleniyor. Bu rakamların arkasında artan yaşam maliyetleriyle mücadele eden aileler ve borç ödemeleriyle temel kamu hizmetlerinin finansmanı arasında zor tercihler yapmak zorunda kalan hükümetler bulunduğunu belirten Misned, krizin özellikle en fazla etkilenen ülkelerin yıllar içinde elde ettiği kalkınma kazanımlarını tehdit ettiğini kaydetti. Geçici bir krizin uzun vadeli kalkınma engeline dönüşmesinin önlenmesi gerektiğini vurguladı. Katar'dan BM ile 21 milyon dolarlık anlaşma Katar'ın krizlere karşı diplomasi ve kalkınma işbirliğini birlikte yürüttüğünü belirten Misned, ülkesinin 2025 yılında ilgili kurumları aracılığıyla Birleşmiş Milletler (BM) ile toplam 21 milyon dolar değerinde iki anlaşma imzaladığını hatırlattı. Anlaşmaların gıda güvenliği ve en az gelişmiş ülkelerin dayanıklılığının artırılması gibi alanları kapsayan Doha Eylem Programı'nı desteklemeyi amaçladığını söyledi. Misned, krizden en fazla etkilenen ülkelerin artan maliyetlerle mücadele edebilmesi için zamanında ve uygun koşullarda finansmana erişmesi gerektiğini belirterek bu süreçte borç yüklerinin daha da artırılmamasının önemine işaret etti. Doha, 2027'de en az gelişmiş ülkeleri ağırlayacak Katar, 25-27 Mart 2027 tarihlerinde Doha'da En Az Gelişmiş Ülkeler için Doha Eylem Programı'nın üst düzey ara dönem değerlendirme toplantısına ev sahipliği yapacak. Misned, toplantının uluslararası taahhütlerin somut sonuçlara dönüştürülmesi açısından önemli bir fırsat olacağını belirtti. “Mesajımız açıktır. Küresel krizlerin ortaya çıkmasında çok az sorumluluğu bulunan en az gelişmiş ülkeler, bu krizlerin sonuçlarından en fazla etkilenen ülkeler olmamalıdır” diyen Misned, erken harekete geçilmesi, koordinasyonun güçlendirilmesi ve kalkınma kazanımlarının korunması çağrısında bulundu. Katar'ın bu konudaki diyaloğu Aralık 2026'da düzenlenecek Doha Forumu'nda sürdürmesi bekleniyor.

items.title: 'Not the answer': Labour MPs speak out against Rosebank as decision looms
items.summary: There is a growing expectation among senior Labour figures that drilling in the oil field will be given the green light.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: 'Not the answer': Labour MPs speak out against Rosebank as decision looms
items.summaryTr: There is a growing expectation among senior Labour figures that drilling in the oil field will be given the green light.
items.articleText: 'Not the answer': Labour MPs speak out against Rosebank as decision looms - Published Some Labour MPs have called on the government to reject the Rosebank oil field, saying it is "incompatible" with the UK's climate commitments. There is a growing expectation among senior Labour figures that drilling in the oil field off the north-west coast of Shetland will be given the go-ahead. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Wednesday that a decision would be "taken in due course" while Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh stressed that affordability of energy bills was her "overriding objective". But in a sign of the division within the party, more than a dozen Labour MPs expressed concerns in Parliament about approving it. Others expressed support, pointing to economic benefits. Supportive Labour MPs said some other parts of the world emitted far more greenhouse gases than the UK and warned of relying on imports. Reports have suggested that Chancellor John Healey is in favour of approval. Separately, it is understood some Labour backbenchers have organised a letter opposing Rosebank - intended for Burnham, but not yet sent - which more than 60 out of about 400 Labour MPs have indicated they support. One signatory told the BBC that approving Rosebank "would not create new jobs, would bring minimal money into the Treasury and be bad for the climate". "The government's central aim is to tackle the cost of living crisis, and drilling for more oil at Rosebank isn't the answer," the MP said. Wednesday's Westminster Hall - a type of parliamentary debate where backbench MPs raise topical issues but do not vote - was organised by Green MP Carla Denyer. Labour MP for Sheffield Central Abtisam Mohamed told the debate: "Rosebank fails on every test. "It will not benefit taxpayers who will shoulder the vast majority of the development costs, it will not strengthen our energy security because most of the oil will be sold on international markets, and it will not reduce energy bills for our constituents, who will remain exposed to volatile fossil fuel prices." Richard Burgon, a former frontbencher on the left of the party, said: "Rosebank is not compatible with our climate targets - it's dangerous to pretend otherwise." The UK is committed to reaching net zero by 2050 and wants to limit global warming to no more than 1.5C above the pre-industrial period. The UK government has always insisted that Rosebank is a quasi-judicial decision, formally resting with Fahnbulleh. She green-lit production in the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea last month, but Rosebank hangs in the balance. Labour's manifesto upon entering power in 2024 pledged not to "issue new licences to explore new fields". Licences for both Jackdaw and Rosebank were granted by the then Conservative UK government in 2022 and 2023 respectively. But the Court of Session in Edinburgh ruled last year that the government had made the approvals unlawfully, leaving the current Labour government to make a fresh decision on whether to give the go-ahead. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch sought to tease at Labour divisions on the issue during Prime Minister's Questions on Wednesday. Demand for fossil fuels During the debate, Labour MP Anna Gelderd said: "We live in an unprecedented era where our energy security is more vital than ever, in which jobs and wealth must be protected and economic opportunities seized - on both of these points, Rosebank fails." Labour MP Julia Buckley said she had received opposition to Rosebank from her constituents in "regularly flooded Shrewsbury" and said fossil fuels "belong in the past, not the future". She urged Fahnbulleh to "reject the oil licence in favour of renewables", adding: "Please don't add further to our climate emergency." Other Labour MPs expressed their support, including recently departed veterans minister Al Carns, who warned that Britain would continue to need fossil fuels for decades and importing more would be a mistake. "Refusing to produce it here does nothing on its own to eliminate that demand - it simply increases our reliance on imports which can carry their own environmental cost," he added. Those representing communities with ties to the oil and gas industry, including Jonathan Brash, the Labour MP for Hartlepool, stressed the benefits of approving Rosebank for British jobs. Speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live, Labour MP Bill Esterson, chair of Energy Security and Net Zero Committee, said "the economics of it (Rosebank) are that you should carry on with it" and "there's an element of energy security" by approving it. Energy minister Michael Shanks told the debate the government would take a "pragmatic approach" to a clean energy transition, stressing it was "not a turn off the taps government, but nor can we justifiably be a drill every last drop government either". "This government will not make decisions for this country which are not compatible with our climate obligations," he added. - Rosebank: Life on the oil field at the centre of a political storm - Published25 October - Action on energy costs is my overriding aim, says Fahnbulleh - Published2 days ago - Political battle intensifies within Labour over Rosebank oil field - Published26 October Sign up for our Politics Essential newsletter to keep up with the inner workings of Westminster and beyond.

items.title: Nomura explores sale of crypto unit Laser Digital: Bloomberg
items.summary: The potential sale of Laser Digital follows a fourth straight quarterly loss for Nomura’s European operations.

items.titleTr: Nomura explores sale of crypto unit Laser Digital: Bloomberg
items.summaryTr: The potential sale of Laser Digital follows a fourth straight quarterly loss for Nomura’s European operations.
items.articleText: Nomura explores sale of crypto unit Laser Digital: Bloomberg The potential sale of Laser Digital follows a fourth straight quarterly loss for Nomura’s European operations. Japanese financial services giant Nomura Holdings is reportedly weighing a sale of its cryptocurrency subsidiary Laser Digital as Nomura’s European operations continue to post losses. Nomura has held talks with potential buyers, including Marex Group, Bloomberg reported Wednesday. The company has yet to make a final decision and could keep the business, according to the report. Nomura’s European businesses posted a pretax loss of 7.4 billion yen ($46.5 million) in the quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026, their fourth consecutive quarterly loss. The company posted pretax profits in every other reporting region over the same period. Nomura did not disclose whether Laser Digital, which is headquartered in Switzerland, contributed to the European result. Nomura is one of Japan’s largest financial services groups, with its investment management division overseeing 152.8 trillion yen ($960 billion) in assets as of September 2026. The potential sale comes less than three months after Laser Digital Japan secured the country’s first new crypto exchange license in four years, allowing the firm to expand its institutional crypto trading services in Japan. Established in 2022, Laser Digital provides institutional cryptocurrency trading, asset management and venture investment services. The company has also pursued expansion in the United States, receiving preliminary approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency for its proposed national trust bank in May. During a January earnings call, chief financial officer Hiroyuki Moriuchi said the company would reduce its cryptocurrency trading positions to limit short-term volatility while continuing to expand Laser Digital over the medium to long term.
